aliases: Türk Eğitim Vakfı Mesleki Ortaöğretim Bursu
organizer_domain_provenance: NOT INDEPENDENTLY ESTABLISHED BY FETCH. tev.org.tr self-identifies as Türk Eğitim Vakfı, founded 1967, and hosts its own announcement archive and scholarship portal (burs.tev.org.tr) under the same registrable domain. TEV is a Turkish public-benefit foundation (kamuya yararlı vakıf). Attempted corroboration was blocked: burs.tev.org.tr returned ECONNRESET. No .gov.tr page linking to tev.org.tr was fetched in this session. Domain rests on organiser self-attestation plus consistent subdomain control; re-check before ingestion.
grade_range: Mesleki ortaöğretim (vocational secondary / high school) students
prerequisites: NOT VERIFIED ON OFFICIAL PAGE. Widely reported conditions — Turkish citizenship, enrolment in formal (örgün) education in Turkey, not enrolled in open/distance/fee-paying programmes, no sibling already holding the same TEV scholarship, and means-tested income and asset limits — come from Turkish news coverage, NOT from a fetched TEV page. Treat as unverified until the TEV conditions page is read.
financial_aid: The scholarship is itself the financial aid: a monthly stipend.
selection_process: Means-tested plus academic merit. Applications for 2026-2027 are stated to be entirely online. TEV states special provisions exist for students under state protection, students with disabilities, students affected by natural disasters, and Darüşşafaka High School graduates — this detail is from search results, not a fetched official page.
required_materials: Online application form (details published by TEV closer to opening)
source_title: TEV 2026-2027 Burs Başvuru Tarihleri Belli Oldu! – Türk Eğitim Vakfı
research_notes: CURRENT-CYCLE TRAP CAUGHT AND AVOIDED — this is the key note. TEV's site still displays an older announcement titled 'TEV Mesleki Ortaöğretim Bursu başvuruları 2 Ekim'e uzatıldı!' (announcement id 59). Fetching it shows it refers to '18 Ağustos - 2 Ekim 2025' — the 2025-2026 cycle. Reading the homepage alone, or trusting a news snippet, would have produced a wrong 2 October deadline and a wrong 18 August open date. The correct current figures come from announcement id 63: Mesleki Ortaöğretim applications run '1 Eylül - 8 Ekim 2026'. As of the 2026-08-21 retrieval date this cycle has NOT yet opened — it opens in 11 days. VERIFIED from the official announcement: the 2026-2027 date ranges for every TEV scholarship type. AMBIGUITY FLAGGED, NOT RESOLVED: the '3.500 TL' figure for Lise (high school) appears on the official page within what renders as a donation/contribution widget listing sponsorship amounts, not unambiguously as the scholarship payment. Turkish news coverage separately reports 3,500 TL/month as the 2026-2027 vocational-secondary scholarship amount. Because the official rendering is ambiguous I have NOT written an amount into a dedicated field. HIGH VALUE FOR ORYN: Turkey is the top-priority geography, scholarship is a thin category, and this cycle opens within the coming fortnight.

organizer: King Abdulaziz and His Companions Foundation for Giftedness and Creativity (Mawhiba)
organizer_domain_provenance: NOT ESTABLISHED BY FETCH — two government corroboration attempts were blocked. The Saudi national government platform lists the foundation as an agency at https://my.gov.sa/ar/agencies/18305 (HTTP 403 when fetched) and the Saudi Press Agency carries programme announcements at https://www.spa.gov.sa/N2529036 (HTTP 403 when fetched). Both were surfaced via search but neither could be read directly, so neither is being counted as evidence. Supporting-but-weak signal: mawhiba.sa sits on Saudi Arabia's restricted .sa second-level namespace, and the site self-identifies as the foundation. Provenance should be completed before ingestion.
prerequisites: Registration in the National Program for Gifted Identification is a stated prerequisite. Applicants must score 1400 or higher on the Mawhiba Multiple Cognitive Aptitude Test (MMCAT). Students who took the MMCAT in Arabic must additionally meet an English threshold: STEP 75, IELTS 5.5, TOEFL iBT 53, or TOEIC 600.
cost: Full-time SR 3,000 (SR 2,550 with a 15% higher-score discount); part-time SR 1,750 (SR 1,487.50 discounted); online SR 500; partial waiver rate SR 150
financial_aid: Fee waivers may be requested by students receiving social security benefits, students registered with charitable organisations, children of martyrs, and students with verified financial hardship.
selection_process: Nomination-based: students are notified of nomination, then register online and pay the programme fee to confirm enrolment. MMCAT score of 1400+ and National Program for Gifted Identification registration gate eligibility.
required_materials: Online registration; MMCAT score; English test score where the MMCAT was taken in Arabic
award_or_output: Laboratory skills, an actual research project, data analysis and report writing, plus scientific mentorship. Exceptional participants receive a further six months of mentorship through the Mawhiba Mentorship Program.
research_notes: VERIFIED_HISTORICAL rather than VERIFIED_CURRENT because both dates on the official page are already past at the 2026-08-21 retrieval date: the registration deadline was 18 May 2026 and the programme ran 5-30 July 2026. The page is current and accurate; the cycle is simply over. No 2027 dates are published. INTERNATIONAL ELIGIBILITY — verified carefully because it is a high-scrutiny field: the official page states 'The student must be of Saudi nationality or born to a Saudi mother. Non-Saudi students will be admitted, but their number should not exceed 10% of the total student enrollment.' So international_applicants_allowed=true, but with a hard 10% quota, which is why the quota is written into eligible_countries context rather than implied. COST verified in full from the official page including every fee tier and the waiver grounds — this matters because a counsellor recommending it must know the SR 500 online tier exists. Grades 9-11 map to roughly ages 14-17, squarely in ORYN's band.

canonical_name: Mawhiba Skills Enrichment Program in Entrepreneurship and Innovation
organizer: King Abdulaziz and His Companions Foundation for Giftedness and Creativity (Mawhiba), in collaboration with the Small & Medium Enterprises General Authority (Monsha'at)
organizer_domain_provenance: Same as the Mawhiba Research Enrichment Program record: NOT ESTABLISHED BY FETCH. my.gov.sa agency listing (https://my.gov.sa/ar/agencies/18305) and Saudi Press Agency coverage (https://www.spa.gov.sa/N2529036) both returned HTTP 403. Additional supporting signal specific to this record: the official page names Monsha'at, the Saudi government's Small & Medium Enterprises General Authority, as the delivery partner — a government-partnership claim that itself warrants independent confirmation.
prerequisites: MMCAT score of 1400 or higher. Saudi nationality or a Saudi mother; non-Saudis admitted subject to a 10% cap on total intake.
program_dates: 2026-03-28 to 2026-05-23, held on Saturdays 09:00-13:00 (4 hours), 9 weeks total
cost: In-person SAR 500 (SAR 575 incl. VAT); online SAR 300 (SAR 345 incl. VAT); partial exemption SAR 150 (SAR 172.50 incl. VAT)
financial_aid: A partial exemption tier is offered at SAR 150 (SAR 172.50 incl. VAT).
selection_process: MMCAT threshold of 1400+, then registration via the Enrichment Programs Registration Portal during the October-November window.
required_materials: Online registration via the Enrichment Programs Registration Portal; MMCAT score
award_or_output: Development of eight entrepreneurial competencies: business mindset, innovation concepts, marketing, financial literacy, commercial identity design, time management and financial planning. The official page does not describe a specific final deliverable.
research_notes: VERIFIED from the official page: the March-May 2026 delivery dates and Saturday 09:00-13:00 schedule, the full three-tier fee table with and without VAT, the Monsha'at partnership, the MMCAT 1400 threshold, the nationality rule with its 10% non-Saudi cap, and the eight competencies taught. CYCLE REASONING, stated explicitly so it is not mistaken for a verified date: the 2026 delivery (28 March - 23 May 2026) is past at the 2026-08-21 retrieval date, so this is VERIFIED_HISTORICAL. The official page describes registration as running 'October to November each year' — a recurring annual window, not a dated one. It is therefore REASONABLE TO EXPECT the next registration to open around October 2026, roughly six weeks after retrieval, but that is an INFERENCE from the stated annual pattern and no 2026-cycle registration date is published, so the deadline field is left null rather than filled with a guessed October date. WHY THIS RECORD EARNS ITS PLACE: entrepreneurship is one of ORYN's thinnest categories (3 live rows), this is Middle East coverage, and unlike most entrepreneurship offerings it is term-time rather than summer, so it does not compete with the saturated summer-programme pool.

organizer_domain_provenance: NOT INDEPENDENTLY ESTABLISHED BY FETCH. jaeurope.org self-identifies as JA Europe and hosts the programme portfolio. Supporting signal: the EIT Deep Tech Talent Initiative — an EU body under the European Institute of Innovation and Technology — lists JA Europe as a pledger at eitdeeptechtalent.eu and co-brands a Company Programme AI course, which was surfaced via search but NOT fetched. Separately, ORYN already holds the Turkish JA member programme (GençBizz, Genç Başarı Eğitim Vakfı) as a live record, which corroborates the network's national-member structure from inside ORYN's own data.
prerequisites: Delivered through schools — students join via a participating school and teacher, not by individual application. Availability depends on whether the student's country has an active JA member organisation and whether their school runs the programme.
selection_process: No competitive selection at entry; participation is via school enrolment. Within the programme students elect a board of directors from among their peers.
required_materials: None at student level; the school and teacher enrol
award_or_output: Students form and run a real mini-company for an academic year: raising share capital, developing and marketing a product or service, and presenting a report and accounts to shareholders. Top mini-companies progress to the JA Company of the Year competition.
research_notes: AGE DISCREPANCY RESOLVED IN FAVOUR OF THE OFFICIAL PAGE: the fetched jaeurope.org page states the programme targets students aged '15-18'. Multiple secondary sources and search summaries state '15-19'. Since aggregator text is a lead and not evidence, 15-18 is recorded and the discrepancy is logged here rather than averaged or silently resolved. VERIFIED from the official page: the 15-18 age range, the one-academic-year duration, school-mediated delivery, the mini-company mechanics (board election, share capital, report and accounts to shareholders), and the scale figures of 360,000+ students and 30,000 mini-companies annually. NOT ON THE OFFICIAL PAGE and therefore left null: cost to students, the country list, and any dates or deadlines. The frequently-cited '40 European countries' figure came from search results only and is not written into eligible_countries. verification_state is NEEDS_REVIEW because country coverage and cost — the two things a counsellor most needs in order to tell a specific student whether they can actually do this — are both unresolved, and because no cycle dates exist to verify against. STRUCTURAL NOTE FOR ORYN: this is an umbrella network record, not a single bookable opportunity. Its real value is as a parent entity for national member programmes; ORYN already holds the Turkish member (GençBizz). Consider modelling it that way rather than as a directly-applicable opportunity, otherwise the counsellor may recommend something a student has no route into.
